children: Starknet's STRK (STRK-USD) cryptocurrency extended its rally Sunday, rising about 16% as a burst of speculative trading added momentum to the blockchain network's recent push to attract Bitcoin holders. STRK has surged from roughly $0.044 to $0.057 in the past 24 hours, after jumping about 26% Saturday.

The move has been accompanied by a sharp increase in trading. By 12:08 p.m. ET Sunday, CoinGecko showed STRK with more than $240 million in 24-hour volume and a market capitalization of about $427 million. The token has gained more than 35% in the past week and more than doubled in the past month.

The rally accelerated Saturday after a crypto trader using the name Pumponomics posted a bullish STRK thesis on X at about 10:33 a.m. ET, saying he had accumulated about $740,000 of the token during the week. Binance STRK/USDT volume began rising around that time, with the token jumping about 12% during the 11 a.m. hour on unusually heavy trading.

On-chain data also showed a wallet receiving about 17.44 million STRK from Coinbase Prime minutes before the post. The position closely matched one displayed by Pumponomics, though the identity of the wallet's owner couldn't be independently confirmed. Futures trading also surged, with volume rising about 213% to $187.7 million and open interest climbing about 20% to $74.2 million Saturday.
The speculative activity followed an Oct. 2 announcement from Starknet that it would cover bridge fees for the first 100 Bitcoin

moved onto its network through strkBTC. Starknet also highlighted ways holders can stake strkBTC through Endur, provide liquidity through Ekubo Protocol or use it as collateral to borrow USDC through Vesu.

StrkBTC is a Bitcoin-backed token that lets holders use their Bitcoin in applications on Starknet. Users who stake strkBTC through Endur receive xstrkBTC, with rewards paid in STRK and automatically compounded. Starknet cited an annual percentage yield of about 3%. StrkBTC also offers optional shielding to make balances and transactions private.

Starknet is a Layer 2 blockchain built to make Ethereum transactions faster and less expensive. It processes transactions separately and uses cryptographic proofs known as STARKs to verify the results on Ethereum. Unlike many Ethereum scaling networks, Starknet uses its own Cairo programming language. STRK is the network's native token and is used for transaction fees, staking and governance.

For investors, the Bitcoin initiative is significant because Starknet is trying to attract some of Bitcoin's liquidity into its decentralized-finance ecosystem. Rather than competing with Bitcoin, strkBTC is redeemable for native BTC and is intended to make Bitcoin usable for lending, borrowing, liquidity provision and other applications on Starknet.

Another potential catalyst is approaching Monday. Starknet v0.14.4 is scheduled for mainnet deployment Oct. 5, pending governance approval. Starknet describes the release as relatively small and mostly transparent to users, with support for proving unusually large transactions and other technical improvements.

The timing makes it difficult to pin STRK's rally on any single catalyst. Starknet's Bitcoin promotion preceded the move by more than a day, while the sharp breakout came after social-media attention and trading volume suddenly increased Saturday. The subsequent jump in futures activity and STRK's continued rise Sunday suggest momentum traders have become an important part of the rally.
